items.q: Fill up: The first mechanism of renal autoregulation, put in brackets as the stretch reflex, is the ______ reflex.
items.exp: Mechanism: 1. myogenic reflex (stretch reflex); 2. tubulo-glomerular feedback (adenosine mediated). (Book p738)

items.q: On the autoregulation graph, the vertical dashed lines that bracket the plateau are drawn on which axis, and between which values?
opts: Mean arterial blood pressure, between about 80 and 180 mm Hg
Mean arterial blood pressure, between 0 and 40 mm Hg
Renal plasma flow, between 125 and 700 ml/min
items.exp: The plot's x-axis is mean arterial blood pressure (0–240 mm Hg) with the 'autoregulatory range' double arrow spanning roughly 80–180, over the flat portion of the renal blood flow curve. (Book p738)

items.q: Fill up: In the macula densa arm of the flowchart, the rising luminal solute is written as increased NaCl/______ reaching the macula densa.
items.exp: The printed line is '↑ GFR/tubular injury → ↑ NaCl/KCl reach macula densa', followed by adenosine and afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction. (Book p738)

items.q: A patient in pre-renal failure has a falling GFR. Per the left branch of this page's flowchart, the afferent arteriolar response and its effect are:
opts: No response, since autoregulation only answers a raised MAP
items.exp: In response to ↓ GFR the flowchart shows afferent arteriolar vasodilatation (eg: pre-renal failure) → ↑ filtration; the adenosine branch belongs to ↑ GFR/tubular injury. (Book p738)

items.q: Match each branch of the autoregulation flowchart with its printed example or mediator — 1) Response to ↓ GFR 2) ↑ GFR/tubular injury 3) Mediator of tubulo-glomerular feedback … A) Adenosine B) Pre-renal failure C) Acute tubular injury D) Stretch reflex
items.exp: The ↓ GFR branch is illustrated by pre-renal failure; the ↑ GFR/tubular injury branch is illustrated by acute tubular injury and runs through adenosine; the stretch reflex is the myogenic mechanism, a different item. (Book p738)

items.q: In the glomerulo-tubular balance example with GFR = 100 ml/min, the filtered Na+ load and the excreted amount are:
items.exp: GFR = 100 ml/min → Na+ filtered = 100 meq → 99 meq reabsorbed, 1 meq excreted (1%). (Book p738)

items.q: Each of the following is part of the page's glomerulo-tubular balance account EXCEPT:
opts: The percentage of filtered sodium excreted rises as GFR rises
An increase in GFR is followed by increased tubular reabsorption
In the second example 198 meq are reabsorbed and 2 meq excreted, still labelled 1%
items.exp: The whole point of the balance is that the percentage of Na+ excreted remains constant at 1%; the doubling example on the page is 300 meq filtered with 198 reabsorbed and 2 meq excreted. (Book p738)

items.q: Match each axis of the autoregulation graph with its label — 1) X-axis 2) Y-axis … A) Mean arterial blood pressure (mm Hg) B) Flow rate (L/min)
items.exp: The x-axis is labelled 'Mean arterial blood pressure (mm Hg)' from 0–240 and the y-axis 'Flow rate (L/min)' from 0–1.5, with the solid curve labelled 'Renal blood flow' and the dashed low curve 'GFR'. (Book p738)

items.q: In the autoregulation graph, the solid red curve that plateaus in the autoregulatory range is labelled:
items.exp: The solid curve is labelled 'Renal blood flow' and the dashed near-zero curve 'GFR'; both are flat between about 80 and 180 mmHg MAP. (Book p738)
